item.title: Naira appreciates to N1,373/$ in parallel market
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira today appreciated to N1,373 per dollar from N1,380 in the parallel market on Thursday. But the naira was stable at N1,346 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed. Consequently, the margin between the parallel and official markets narrowed to N27 per dollar from N36 per dollar on Thursday. The value of interbank turnover in NFEM increased by 8.9 per cent to $58.9 billion from $54.05 billion on Thursday. Analysts expect the mixed performance of the naira in the following weeks. In their financial market review and outlook, analysts at Cowry Asset Management Limited said, “Going forward, we expect the naira to remain relatively mixed across the foreign exchange markets in the near term, supported by marginal improvements in external reserves and potential foreign exchange inflows. “However, sustained pressure on foreign currency demand could limit further gains.” The post Naira appreciates to N1,373/$ in parallel market appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US midterm early voting hits record 48 million
item.description: A record 47.9 million Americans have already voted in next week’s US midterm elections, with participation surging in key battleground states and registered Democrats outpacing Republicans, figures showed Friday. The University of Florida’s Election Lab had recorded 47,922,669 early votes nationwide by midday, surpassing the previous midterm record of 45.9 million cast ahead of Election Day in 2022. The surge is especially pronounced in states with fiercely contested Senate races that could determine control of the chamber during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s presidency. In Texas, more than six million people had voted early by Wednesday, according to official figures, with in-person turnout running around 50 percent ahead of the same stage in 2022. North Carolina’s election board reported early voting up nearly 37 percent on the same point four years ago, while South Carolina surpassed its entire 2022 early vote total on Monday, with five days of early voting still to go. In Kansas, where Republican Senator Roger Marshall faces a tough re-election fight, advance ballots were running around two-thirds ahead of 2022 last week, according to the secretary of state’s office. In states that record voters’ party affiliation, registered Democrats have accounted for a substantially larger share of early ballots than Republicans. Election Lab figures showed Democrats making up around 44 percent of early voters in those states, compared with 31 percent for Republicans and 25 percent for unaffiliated or minor-party voters. University of Florida political scientist Michael McDonald, who oversees the Election Lab, has pointed to rising participation among Black and Hispanic voters in states that report racial and ethnic data, with particularly strong turnout in heavily Hispanic communities along the Texas-Mexico border. In Georgia, where early in-person voting broke the state’s midterm record on Thursday, women accounted for 56 percent of ballots cast by that day, compared with 44 percent for men. “Georgians continue to head to the polls in record numbers because they trust the system,” top elections official Brad Raffensperger said Thursday. But experts warn against interpreting the figures as a prediction of the election outcome. A voter’s party registration does not reveal which candidates they supported, and tens of millions more Americans are expected to cast ballots on Tuesday. In recent elections Republicans have tended to turn out in greater numbers on Election Day, potentially narrowing or reversing the Democrats’ early advantage. And higher early participation does not necessarily translate into higher overall turnout, since some voters may simply be casting ballots sooner than in previous elections. item.title: Ebola outbreak not under control in Africa, CDC warns
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) has warned that the Ebola outbreak spreading across parts of Africa remains uncontrolled, with more than 10,200 confirmed cases and over 5,000 deaths recorded across the continent. The Director-General of Africa CDC, Jean Kaseya, gave the warning on Friday during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief programme, raising concerns about the continued transmission and changing geographical spread of the disease. Kaseya said the assessment followed a virtual ministerial meeting held on October 28, which brought together more than 42 ministers and over 600 participants, including representatives of international organisations and development partners, to review the outbreak and ongoing response efforts. “We analysed the data and we saw that the outbreak is not yet under control,” he said. He disclosed that the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) had recorded more than 10,000 confirmed infections, while the combined number of confirmed cases across the continent had exceeded 10,200. “We have achieved what is a number of 10,000 people confirmed cases in DRC and also, if we put together, it’s more than 10,200 confirmed cases across the continent,” Kaseya said. Kaseya said more than 5,000 people had died from the outbreak, although figures published by health authorities showed a slightly lower confirmed death toll. “We also saw that we have more than 5,000 people already passed on due to this outbreak,” he added. Kaseya also expressed concern over changes in the geographical spread of the disease, noting that its epicentre was shifting. The current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus and has affected several African countries, including the DRC, Kenya and Nigeria. The DRC remains the worst-affected country, accounting for the overwhelming majority of infections and deaths. Data from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control showed that the country had recorded 10,193 confirmed cases and 4,960 related deaths as of October 28. Kenya has also reported nine confirmed cases, including two deaths, following an imported infection linked to the DRC. Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade on October 20, after a 42-year-old Swiss woman tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain in Abuja. The woman, who had travelled from Uganda to Nigeria, was isolated and treated by Nigerian health workers before being medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26 for further treatment after her condition stabilised. Her husband, who was identified as a close contact, was also evacuated. Following their evacuation, the World Health Organisation (WHO) Regional Director for Africa, Mohamed Janabi, said Nigeria had no confirmed Ebola cases. item.title: 2027: INEC has no preferred candidate, party — Amupitan
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has declared that it has no preferred candidate or political party for the 2027 general elections, pledging to uphold the rule of law and the will of Nigerian voters. INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, stated this on Friday when he received a pre-election fact-finding mission of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), led by former Sierra Leone Vice-President, Victor Bockarie Foh, in Abuja. Amupitan said the commission was conducting a readiness assessment tour across the country’s geopolitical zones as part of preparations for the 2027 general elections. “INEC under my watch has no candidate and no political party,” he said. “Our sole allegiance is to the rule of law, the sovereign will of the Nigerian electorate, and the democratic progress of our nation.” The INEC chairman disclosed that the elections would be conducted across 8,809 registration areas and 774 local government areas in the country. He said Nigeria’s voter register had surpassed 103 million, adding that the commission had completed nine of the 14 major statutory milestones outlined in its revised election timetable. According to him, INEC had also concluded three phases of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise and completed the nationwide physical display of the preliminary voter register. On the technology to be deployed for the elections, Amupitan said the commission would use the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) for fingerprint and facial biometric accreditation, alongside electronic result management systems. He added that INEC had introduced the eEC8A electronic verification platform to complement its result management process and verification through the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV). The chairman further said the commission was working with relevant security agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) to ensure adequate security during the polls. Speaking on behalf of the ECOWAS mission, Foh said the visit was part of the regional body’s efforts to assess electoral preparedness in member states approaching general elections. He said the mission, which included Serigne Mamadou Ka, head of the ECOWAS Electoral Assistance Division, would evaluate the preparedness of electoral stakeholders and identify areas where the regional body could offer support. Foh explained that the exercise was being conducted in line with Article 31 of the ECOWAS Protocol on Democracy and Good Governance and Article 53 of the ECOWAS Conflict Prevention Framework. item.title: US woman who survived botched execution says she’s in constant pain
item.description: Convicted murderer Christa Pike said Friday that she is in constant pain, a month after surviving a botched execution attempt in the US state of Tennessee. “There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain,” Pike said in a statement released by her lawyers. “My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts,” she said. “I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul.” Pike, 50, was given two doses of the drug pentobarbital at a state prison on September 30 — a usually fatal dose that nevertheless failed to kill her. She was transported to hospital in critical condition and returned to prison after receiving medical treatment. Pike is the only inmate to ever survive after being injected with lethal doses of execution drugs, according to the Death Penalty Information Center. Pike was sentenced to death in Tennessee after she and her boyfriend beat and killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer at a job training camp. Pike was 18 at the time of the murder. In her statement, Pike said she is recovering “but healing is not the same as being okay.” “I don’t know why I survived that night,” she said. “I don’t know what comes next. Some days, finding hope is harder than others. For now, I am trying to heal, one day at a time.” Since the botched execution, Pike’s lawyers have repeatedly called on Tennessee Governor Bill Lee to commute her sentence to life in prison. Lee, a Republican, has suspended executions in Tennessee pending an independent investigation. Asked by reporters this week about Pike’s fate, Lee said: “I suspect her sentence will be the same as it was before unless determined otherwise by the courts.” There have been 32 executions in the United States this year, all by lethal injection. The death penalty has been abolished in 23 of the 50 US states, while three others — California, Oregon and Pennsylvania — have moratoriums in place. item.title: ‘This isn’t Disneyland’ – Arteta warns Dowman after red card incident
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Mikel Arteta has warned Max Dowman to control his emotions after the 16-year-old Arsenal forward was sent off in the Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town. According to Sky Sports, Dowman was dismissed for violent conduct after appearing to kick out at Harrison Neal following a strong challenge. Arsenal later exited the competition on penalties. As Dowman headed towards the tunnel, Arteta spoke to him in the heat of the moment. Sky Sports pundit Paul Merson criticised the exchange, saying the Arsenal manager should have put an arm around the teenager. Arteta defended his response, saying young players must meet the demands of top-level football. “What do you expect? That’s the level and that’s the reaction. Whether it’s right or wrong, that’s the reaction. And the reaction when I don’t win, I’m ** off, big time. “This is the environment and the reality. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League. We look after him so much, but we are also demanding, as he needs to earn the right to play. Otherwise, what are the rest of the boys going to tell me?” Arteta further said his reaction came from frustration and concern about the consequences Dowman could face. He added that they had discussed the teenager’s discipline before the match, following a similar incident with England earlier in the month. “It will continue to happen with the way he plays and the way he attracts opponents,” Arteta said. “We have to be protective of him, as he is 16, but also very straight with him about what to expect from him towards the team and the club.” Arteta said he had spoken with Dowman the previous day and insisted there was no lasting issue between them. “There are no issues at all,” he said. “We’ve all made these mistakes. We know how much you can get punished and what happens next. It’s not the first time, so we need to put an end to it very quickly.” The post ‘This isn’t Disneyland’ – Arteta warns Dowman after red card incident appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘Daddy loves you specially,’ — D’banj remembers late son eight years after death
item.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian music star Oladapo Daniel Oyebanjo, popularly known as D’banj, has paid an emotional tribute to his late son, Daniel Oyebanjo III, eight years after his tragic death. The singer took to his Instagram page to remember the toddler, fondly known as Daniel D3rd, expressing his enduring love for him and reflecting on how the family has continued to cope with the loss. In his tribute, D’banj said he missed his son but expressed gratitude that he, his wife and their other children were now in a safe place. “I miss you Daniel D3rd my son and trust me I can’t imagine how your mother feels but we are in a Safe Space now THANK YOU …” he wrote. The entertainer also described Daniel as the family’s star boy, adding that the experience had taught him important lessons about life. “Omo Baba Eh, our family’s star boy. “But thank you I’m in a Safe space and so is your mother and your brother and sister, I’m sure you are Proud of us. “Thank you for Showing me what life Really is as a WHOLE.” D’banj further remembered his late uncle, Femi, in the tribute, asking his son to pass a message to him. “Say hi to your Uncle Femi, telll him I miss him too.” Expressing his affection for the deceased toddler, the singer added: “Daddy loves you Specially, Physically, Spiritually and Powerfully.” He signed off the message as “Your Dad Daniel D2nd Lee, The No 1 Entertainer Ever liveth.” Daniel died on June 24, 2018, at the age of 13 months after reportedly drowning in a swimming pool at the family’s residence in Ikoyi, Lagos. His death deeply affected D’banj and his wife, Lineo Didi Kilgrow, who have since continued to rebuild their lives following the devastating incident. The singer’s latest tribute has drawn emotional reactions from fans and well-wishers, many of whom have expressed sympathy and support for the family. item.title: Sowore, police clash over account of attack in Ekiti
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela & Ayobami Okerinde The presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, has disputed the Ekiti State Police Command’s account of an incident in which he sustained injuries at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, insisting that he and his associates were attacked by suspected political thugs. The police had dismissed reports that Sowore was kidnapped by armed men in the state capital, describing the incident as an altercation with some individuals at a restaurant around the Dalimore area of the state. However, Sowore, in a post on X on Friday, accused the police of downplaying the incident, rejecting the description of the attack as an altercation. He accompanied the post with a video allegedly showing Ekiti State Commissioner of Police, Falade Adegoroye Michael, leaving what appeared to be a hospital emergency room after visiting him. Sowore wrote, “The Commissioner of @PoliceNG in Ekiti State, CP Falade Adegoroye Michael, personally visited the scene of the brutal attack against us in Ado-Ekiti today. He saw firsthand the extensive injuries we sustained, yet he has the audacity to issue a despicable statement describing a coordinated, violent attack as a mere ‘altercation.’ “THERE WAS NO ALTERCATION! WE WERE ATTACKED! “The Commissioner saw the injuries, witnessed the aftermath of the violence, and was fully aware of the seriousness of what happened. Yet his Command has chosen to trivialize the attack, even describing the injuries as ‘minor.” Earlier, Sowore had raised the alarm in another post on X, claiming that he had been kidnapped by armed thugs and that his whereabouts were unknown. The Ekiti State Police Command, however, dismissed the claim in a statement issued by its Public Relations Officer, Sunday Abutu, saying preliminary information indicated that Sowore had an altercation with some individuals at a restaurant. According to the police, officers were alerted and swiftly mobilised to the scene, where they rescued Sowore and took him to the Police Hospital in Ado-Ekiti for medical attention. The statement read, “The attention of the Ekiti State Police Command has been drawn to a message circulating on social media alleging that Mr. Omoyele Sowore, the African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate in the forthcoming presidential election, was kidnapped by armed thugs in Ado-Ekiti, with his whereabouts unknown. “The Command wishes to categorically clarify that Mr. Sowore was not kidnapped. Rather, preliminary information indicates that he had an altercation with some individuals at a restaurant around Dalimore area, Ado-Ekiti, following which the Police were immediately alerted. “Upon receiving the report, Police operatives swiftly mobilised to the scene and successfully rescued him. item.title: Trump reinstates rallies in Kansas, Iowa before midterms
item.description: US President Donald Trump has put campaign rallies in Kansas and Iowa back on the schedule for Sunday — two days before the midterm elections — after abruptly canceling both appearances, a Republican source told AFP Friday. “The rallies are back on. President Trump loves his supporters, and in addition to nearly 20 tele-rallies, he will hold back-to-back rallies in Kansas and Iowa on Sunday,” a party source familiar with Trump’s weekend planning said. Trump had originally been scheduled to campaign in Salina, Kansas, on Saturday and Dubuque, Iowa, on Sunday, but both appearances were scrapped on Thursday, with Republicans saying he would instead concentrate on telephone rallies. The sudden changes raised questions about the 80-year-old president’s health and stamina, prompting an angry response when a reporter asked whether he was feeling well. “I feel perfect,” Trump snapped, saying he no longer needed to visit Kansas because Republican Senator Roger Marshall was “doing very well.” Marshall faces an unexpectedly competitive challenge from Democrat Adam Hamilton in Kansas, which has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932. In Iowa, Republican congresswoman Ashley Hinson is fighting a close race against Democrat Josh Turek. Both states voted comfortably for Trump in 2024, but have emerged as battlegrounds in the fight for control of the Senate. Republicans are defending their 53-47 majority in the Senate in Tuesday’s elections, while Democrats are seeking to capture at least one chamber of Congress and curb Trump’s legislative agenda during his final two years in office. Political strategist Mike Fahey, a veteran of multiple election campaigns, told AFP Trump’s about-face was likely the result of the questions over his energy levels. “My suspicion is that Trump didn’t particularly like that narrative, and putting the events back on the calendar was the fastest way to kill it,” he said. “There’s also a legitimate campaign strategy argument here… A phone call doesn’t generate the same local headlines, television coverage or excitement as Air Force One landing in your state three days before an election.” The post Trump reinstates rallies in Kansas, Iowa before midterms appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: How Young Nigerians Are Building Businesses Before They Raise Money
item.description: “Zero-capital business” is a loose description. Mobile data, transport, electricity, and time all cost money, and no national dataset shows how many Nigerian firms literally started from nothing. The clearer trend is different: more young people are trying to make a first sale before taking a loan, renting a shop, or filling a storeroom. Moniepoint’s 2025 informal-economy report found that 38% of operators went into business because they could not find work, while its earlier research put 57.7% of informal-business owners below age 34. Credit Is Still an Expensive First Step The Central Bank of Nigeria cut its Monetary Policy Rate to 23% in September 2026 after leaving it at 26.5% in July. That rate is not the same as the borrowing cost a small trader sees at street level, but it still shapes credit conditions across the system. At the same time, 79% of informal businesses surveyed by Moniepoint said their operating costs had risen over the previous year. For a first-time founder, taking on debt before finding customers can be a rough way to begin. Sell Something Before Buying Something Service work has changed the order in which money gets spent. A video editor, developer, designer, or social-media manager can land a project before paying for inventory, and Nigeria’s 3MTT program has been training people in software development, product design, data analysis, cybersecurity, and digital marketing. In October 2025, the 3MTT–NJFP Placement Initiative began linking trained talent with employers at no recruitment or onboarding cost to participating firms. Skills can now be tested in the market before the business has much of a balance sheet. One Phone Can Handle the First Customer For many young founders, the first storefront is a chat thread. Orders come in on WhatsApp, product photos sit on Instagram, and a bank transfer can close the deal before anyone pays for shelves, rent, or a cashier’s desk. Moniepoint found that cash still dominates many customer purchases, but 48% of informal-business owners said they preferred transfers when paying other businesses. The same habit of doing more on one device shows up in consumer platforms too: an adult using Melbet can move between sports markets and casino products on a phone instead of going to a betting shop, though any personal play still belongs in a separate entertainment bankroll, not in business cash. Pre-Orders Let Demand Speak First A lot of young sellers now ask the market a question before they spend real money on stock. A fashion seller can collect deposits before buying fabric, and a food vendor can cook against booked deliveries instead of guessing how many walk-in customers might appear. That caution fits the numbers: Moniepoint’s 2025 survey found that 44% of informal businesses reported daily revenue below ₦20,000. item.title: South African court sets limits on anti-migrant demonstration
item.description: Hundreds of protesters gathered outside a court in South Africa’s coastal city of Durban on Friday as the government sought judicial intervention to rein in anti-migrant demonstrations that have turned deadly, leaving one person dead last week. Durban, the Zulu heartland, has emerged as a focal point of anti-migrant agitation led by the March and March movement, which has organised demonstrations against undocumented foreigners across the country for months. Some demonstrations have turned violent, including last week when a mob of about 50 people beat a foreign national to death, prompting President Cyril Ramaphosa to deploy more than 500 soldiers to support the police. Protesters sang and chanted outside the high court, waving placards reading “reclaim our country” and sticks as police officers kept a close watch. Supporters of several political parties, including the centre-right ActionSA and the uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) party led by former president Jacob Zuma, also turned out in solidarity. Judge Peter Olsen allowed March and March movement to proceed with its planned demonstrations, but under tighter conditions following amendments to the government’s application. Under the revised terms, the group may march between 9am and 3pm, with participants barred from carrying weapons or covering their faces. The group was also prohibited from destroying property or setting fire to buildings. The matter is expected to return to court next year. The court action was brought by acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia, who was seeking to stop the demonstrations on the grounds that they threaten public order and the safety of foreign nationals. He cited police intelligence about an alleged plot to set fire to the Home Affairs Refugee Reception Centre in Berea, an inner-city suburb of Durban where asylum seekers go to seek documentation. The unrest has been fuelled by misinformation about a July Constitutional Court ruling that asylum seekers cannot be denied access to South Africa’s asylum system solely on procedural grounds, according to the police. – ‘Widespread violence’ – Counsel for the police told the court on Friday that the situation in Durban had “degenerated into lawlessness” that reactive policing could no longer contain. More than 400 police officers had been deployed, but this had “proved structurally unable to stem the widespread violence”, they said. March and March defended its right to demonstrate under the constitution, distancing itself from the violence and insisting it should not be held responsible for the actions of those involved. “The agenda is to try and silence the people,” March and March legal representative Xolani Zuma told reporters ahead of the court decision. “The real problem are illegal immigrants who are here in the country and terrorising people,” he said. item.title: Nigeria, Russia Review 1967 Bilateral Air Services Agreement
item.description: Nigeria on Friday met with the Russian Federation on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, Russia, as both countries move to strengthen aviation relations and expand cooperation in the air transport sector. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, led Nigeria’s delegation to a high-level bilateral meeting. At the meeting, the Nigerian delegation, led by Keyamo, held discussions with Dmitry Stanislavovich Zverev, who is the State Secretary and Deputy Minister of Transport of the Russian Federation, on the need to modernise the existing framework governing air services between the two countries. A major outcome of the meeting was the resolution by both sides to renegotiate the Bilateral Air Services Agreement (BASA) between Nigeria and Russia, which dates back to 1967, with a view to establishing a new agreement that reflects contemporary developments and emerging opportunities in international aviation. The meeting centred on the need to modernise the existing framework governing air services between the two countries. According to a statement by the aviation ministry, both countries agreed on a six-month timeline to conclude the negotiations and sign the new agreement in Saint Petersburg, Russia, in April 2027. To facilitate the process, the two sides have constituted their respective negotiating teams to commence work immediately and ensure that the agreed timeline is met. “The proposed agreement is expected to provide an updated framework for bilateral air transport relations and create opportunities for enhanced connectivity, closer institutional collaboration and mutually beneficial engagement between the aviation sectors of both countries,” the statement signed by the minister’s Special Adviser on Media and Communications, Tunde Moshood. The Nigerian delegation included the Director-General of the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), Capt. Chris Najomo; the Registrar of the Nigerian College of Aviation Technology (NCAT), Dr. Danjuma Adamu Ismaila, as well as directors from the Federal Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development and the NCAA. “Beyond the review of the existing air services agreement, the meeting also explored other potential areas of cooperation between Nigeria and Russia,” the statement disclosed. It added that both parties expressed their commitment to examining the opportunities in the coming months, with a view to deepening bilateral relations and identifying areas of shared interest in aviation and related sectors. item.title: Pope Leo makes history with US midterm vote
item.description: Pope Leo XIV, the Catholic Church’s first US-born pontiff, has voted in the United States midterm elections, the first known time a pope has voted in a political election. The head of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics, who has clashed with US President Donald Trump, submitted his mail-in ballot in Chicago, the Vatican said Friday. The Chicago-born pontiff “has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen, whenever he was eligible to do so” and believes in “the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes,” it said. A rift earlier this year between US President Donald Trump and the pope sparked global headlines. Leo and Trump repeatedly clashed over papal criticism of the harsh crackdown on immigration in the United States and of the war on Iran, with Trump calling the pontiff “weak” on crime and “terrible” on foreign policy. The pope said he was “not afraid” of Trump. In April, after Trump’s threat to destroy Iran, Leo called on everyone to do their part for peace, urging them to “contact the authorities — political leaders, congressmen — to ask them, to tell them, to work for peace and to reject war and violence.” The crucial US midterm elections are scheduled to be held on November 3. In September, Leo urged the faithful to shake off “all passivity and indifference” toward current events. “We cannot remain as unengaged spectators; rather, we must listen with our hearts, allow ourselves to be challenged, and become involved,” he said during the weekly general audience in St Peter’s Square. Robert Francis Prevost, as he was known before his papal election, voted in Democratic primaries in 2008 and 2010 and in three Republican primaries in the years that followed, according to the New York Times, citing state and local records. In primary elections in Illinois, voters may choose any party’s ballot at the polls, and Prevost varied in his selection, it said. Prevost spent nearly two decades as a missionary in Peru and has both US and Peruvian citizenship. “The Holy Father has also confirmed that, during his years of residence in Peru he exercised his right to vote whenever he was eligible to do so,” the Vatican said. item.title: 2027: Atiku’s son unveils plan for Tinubu’s re-election
item.description: Alhaji Abba Abubakar, son of former Vice-President Atiku, on Friday unveiled his 2027 mobilisation plan in the six geo-political zones for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu. The former vice-president’s son who is the founder and chairman of Haske Bola Tinubu Organisation (HBTO) a political mobilisation and support platform in Abuja at the All Progressives Congress (APC) National Secretariat had earlier defected to the party. “Looking ahead, HBTO is preparing for an ambitious nationwide political mobilisation programme. “As part of this strategy, we intend to commence a two-million-man mobilisation march across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones, beginning from Abuja. “Our immediate mobilisation efforts will focus on supporting the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, whom we recognise as a key political leader in our mobilisation structure in the collective effort to secure Tinubu’s victory in the FCT in 2027. “We are also working in alignment with the FCT minister’s political objective of delivering both the FCT and Rivers for President Tinubu in the forthcoming election,” Abubakar said. The former vice-president’s son added that his organisation was preparing for a major political mobilisation in Rivers in the first week of November. He added that as part of its commitment to complement the Tinubu reform agenda with practical interventions, his organisation was introducing a transportation support initiative through the initial provision of ten luxury buses. He said the initiative was designed to ease transportation challenges, reduce the burden of commuting on ordinary Nigerians and demonstrate that political support must go beyond rhetoric to include tangible contributions to the lives of citizens. “We intend to commence this programme in the FCT before progressively expanding the initiative to other parts of the federation. “For us, supporting the president’s Renewed Hope Agenda must translate into meaningful actions that positively affect the everyday lives of Nigerians,” he said. According to him, his organisation’s structures are already being activated, and its members are on the ground while its supporters are ready to demonstrate its strength and reach. “This is not simply about numbers or political appearances, it is about building a disciplined, coordinated and effective grassroots mobilisation network capable of translating political support into electoral results. He said the organisation intends to establish its presence across the geopolitical zones, strengthen its state and zonal structures, engage community stakeholders and work collaboratively with other progressive political forces to ensure Tinubu’s re-election. He said political conviction was a matter of personal judgement, conscience and the freedom of every individual to make independent choices. item.title: Flick praises Yamal ‘mentality’ after missing out on Ballon d’Or
item.description: Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal has “reacted very well” following the disappointment of the Ballon d’Or being awarded to Harry Kane, his coach Hansi Flick said on Friday. Despite winning La Liga with the Catalan club and lifting the World Cup with Spain, the 19-year-old winger came third in the vote for the best player in the world on Monday, behind Kane and Kylian Mbappe. “Harry Kane deserved it, but you already know what I think about Lamine. He’s at the level required to win this award,” Flick said ahead of the La Liga leaders’ home match against Alaves. “I’m very proud of Lamine. He reacted very well and was very focused in training. “That’s the way to respond. His mentality is very good for the team.” Yamal will have a chance to put any lingering disappointment behind him on Saturday when Barcelona will look to correct course at home to Alaves following two high-profile defeats. After winning their first 11 matches in all competitions, Barcelona were flying but then came undone when they travelled to PSG in the Champions League last Tuesday. That 4-2 reverse in the French capital was swiftly followed up by a Kylian Mbappe-inspired 2-1 loss at home to Real Madrid in La Liga last weekend. “The most important thing tomorrow is to win,” Flick said. “The team is playing well and we believe in our strengths. I’ve seen a good training session and a positive mood. We have to show that tomorrow. “Alaves are a team that know how to defend well, but we’re Barca and we want to show our best version.” Barcelona still hold a two-point lead at the top of La Liga ahead of their meeting with Atletico Madrid. While the German coach admitted he does not like losing, he insisted that the campaign is “a long road”. “It’s at the end of the season that we can win trophies,” he added. “We have to deal with it. We could have won, but we have to accept defeat and learn from it.” The post Flick praises Yamal ‘mentality’ after missing out on Ballon d’Or appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria, Russia target April 2027 for new air services agreement
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, and Russian officials have agreed to a six-month timeline to modernise the existing framework governing air services between Russia and Nigeria. The agreement was reached during a meeting on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, Russia. At the meeting, the Nigerian delegation, led by Keyamo, held discussions with Dmitry Stanislavovich Zverev, State Secretary and Deputy Minister of Transport of the Russian Federation. The two sides agreed to renegotiate the Bilateral Air Services Agreement, BASA, between Nigeria and Russia, which dates back to 1967, with a view to establishing a new agreement that reflects contemporary developments and emerging opportunities in international aviation. Special Adviser on Media and Communications to the Minister, Tunde Moshood, in a statement, said the proposed agreement was expected to provide an updated framework for bilateral air transport relations and create opportunities for enhanced connectivity, closer institutional collaboration and mutually beneficial engagement between the aviation sectors of both countries. The statement reads: “Both countries agreed on a six-month timeline to conclude the negotiations and sign the new agreement in Saint Petersburg, Russia, in April 2027. To facilitate this process, the two sides have constituted their respective negotiating teams to commence work immediately and ensure that the agreed timeline is met. “The Nigerian delegation included the Director-General of the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, Capt. Chris Najomo; the Registrar of the Nigerian College of Aviation Technology, NCAT, Dr Danjuma Adamu Ismaila; as well as directors from the Federal Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development and the NCAA. “Beyond the review of the existing air services agreement, the meeting also explored other potential areas of cooperation between Nigeria and Russia. Both parties expressed their commitment to examining these opportunities in the coming months, with a view to deepening bilateral relations and identifying areas of shared interest in aviation and related sectors.” The post Nigeria, Russia target April 2027 for new air services agreement appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Sowunmi challenges Utomi over claim Obi will strengthen naira to N500/$1
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Segun Sowunmi, has faulted Pat Utomi’s claim that Peter Obi could strengthen the naira to ₦500 per dollar if elected president. In a post on X on Friday, Sowunmi described the proposal as “a textbook example of confusing political aspiration with economic feasibility” and questioned how the exchange-rate target and promised price cuts would be achieved. Utomi, a political economist and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), had said the target would feature in Obi’s manifesto. “We are convinced that targeting a strategic appreciation of the exchange rate by reasonably strengthening it from ₦1,350/$ to ₦500/$ as part of our manifesto is a winning strategy,” he wrote on X on Thursday. He said the proposal would help curb inflation, reduce poverty and lower the cost of living. With investments in security, electricity and roads, alongside market reforms, Utomi projected that prices of staples including bread, rice, yam, maize, plantain, chicken, eggs and garri could fall by about half. Reacting, Sowunmi asked how the government would secure enough foreign exchange to sustain the proposed rate. “Where is the additional foreign exchange coming from? What will finance the proposed intervention?” he asked. He said exchange rates are shaped by “foreign-exchange supply and demand, productivity, export earnings, capital flows, monetary conditions and confidence in the economy”. He added that the listed commodities had “fundamentally different cost structures” and that a stronger naira “cannot automatically halve the cost of domestically produced commodities”. Sowunmi also disputed Utomi’s cement projection, saying a $10 bag would cost ₦5,000 at ₦500 to the dollar, not ₦2,000. “To arrive at ₦2,000, the authors have additionally assumed a 60% reduction in the dollar-denominated price. Where is the economic justification for that assumption?” he said. He warned that currency appreciation without productivity gains could make imports more attractive and weaken local manufacturers. A serious manifesto, he said, must explain how its policies would work, including their assumptions, costs, timelines and measurable targets. Sowunmi said reducing living costs and poverty was a legitimate ambition, but required productivity growth, stronger agriculture and industry, reliable electricity, infrastructure, security, job creation and sound economic management. “The naira should become stronger because the Nigerian economy has become stronger, not because somebody has decided that ₦500 to the dollar would make an attractive manifesto headline,” he added. item.title: Reps decry encroachment, vandalism of NDPHC’s power transmission projects
item.description: …Threaten removal of illegal structures on transmission routes By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The House of Representatives Committee on Public Assets has decried the encroachment on and vandalism of power transmission projects being executed by the Niger Delta Power Holding Company (NDPHC), warning that illegal structures along designated routes threaten investments in the power sector. Chairman of the committee, Hon. Kuye Ademorin, stated this after inspection visits to the 132kV New Haven-Ninth Mile-Nsukka Double Circuit Transmission Line in Enugu State and the Egbu 330/132/33kV substation in Owerri, Imo State. Other lawmakers on the inspection tour were Hon. Mark Obetta, Hon. Lanre Okunlola, Hon. Sani Rigo and Hon. Canice Moore Nwachukwu. The committee observed that churches, hotels, private residences and state government buildings had been erected along designated transmission routes, raising concerns about project delays and the protection of public assets. Ademorin expressed disappointment that such developments had been allowed despite the Federal Government’s existing rights of way for the transmission projects. He said the encroachment had undermined efforts to expand electricity infrastructure, improve power supply and stimulate industrial development, while vandalism had further threatened government investments. “We observed the magnitude of investment by the Federal Government in building a sustainable power system for the country, particularly in our states, to help them develop their industrial base through adequate power supply. “However, to our chagrin and disappointment, we saw a people who are not totally buying into the vision of a greater country for all of us,” he said. The lawmaker called for stronger collaboration between federal and state authorities to address encroachment, protect public infrastructure and ensure timely completion of ongoing projects. He also urged the government to prioritise project delivery, ensure contractors received timely payments and provide prompt compensation to landowners to prevent disputes and litigation over acquired land. NDPHC disclosed that the Owerri substation, which is about 85 per cent complete, would add approximately 250 megawatts to electricity supply in Imo State and significantly improve power supply to the Orlu area. The project, first awarded in 2006, has received renewed attention under the leadership of NDPHC Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Engr. Jennifer Adighije. Commending the quality of work at the substation, Ademorin expressed optimism that its expected completion around March 2027 would boost industrial activities across the South-East. He appealed to the governors of Enugu and Imo states to work with NDPHC to tackle encroachment, safeguard federal assets and accelerate project delivery. item.title: NDC defends Obi’s single-term pledge, dismisses Okorocha’s ‘gambling’ claim
item.description: By Henry Umoru The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC has thrown its weight behind the single-term presidential pledge by its Presidential candidate ahead of January 16 2027. Peter Obi. The NDC described describing it as a constitutional commitment to performance, national stability and leadership accountability rather than a political gamble, adding that Obi had voluntarily offered to serve only one term, subjecting his leadership to public assessment based on results rather than political calculations. The party noted that Nigeria’s experience with an eight-year presidential administration between 2015 and 2023 demonstrated that longevity in office did not automatically translate into improved governance or national development, adding that the period was characterised by rising inflation, naira depreciation, increasing public debt, widespread poverty and insecurity In a statement signed on Friday by NDC Director-General of the National Presidential Campaign Council, NPCC, Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim, the party disagreed with Okorocha’s characterisation of the pledge as “a four-year gambling”, insisting that the proposal was constitutionally permissible and represented a deliberate commitment to deliver measurable results within four years. According to him, Section 135(2) of the 1999 Constitution provides for a four-year presidential tenure with the possibility of seeking another term, arguing that the provision does not make a second term compulsory. The leadership of the NDC was reacting to comments by former Imo State Governor, Senator Rochas Okorocha, during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he described Obi as “a fantastic gentleman; clear in his head” but questioned the viability of his proposed single-term presidency. The party maintained that Obi’s single-term proposal was designed to shift the focus of presidential leadership from the duration of stay in office to measurable achievements and effective delivery of campaign promises. Describing the pledge as a performance commitment, He said, “Section 135(2) of the 1999 Constitution provides that a President shall leave office after four years and may seek a further four years. In law, ‘may’ is permissive, not mandatory. A single term is therefore constitutional. It is not a gamble. “Nigeria already tested an eight-year tenure between 2015 and 2023. The result was rising inflation, a weakened naira, soaring public debt, widespread poverty, and insecurity across the country. That is the real balance sheet of prolonged tenure without performance. “Peter Obi’s offer is a performance bond, not a gamble. item.title: [VIDEO] N70,000 Allowance: Ajaero Cannot Negotiate On Behalf Of Organised Labour — Osifo
item.description: The President of the Trade Union Congress (TUC), Festus Osifo, has said his Nigerian Labour Congress (NLC) counterpart, Joe Ajaero, cannot negotiate on behalf of organised labour, insisting that he can only speak for NLC members. Osifo spoke on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Friday, following the disagreement between the two labour leaders over the Federal Government’s proposed ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance for workers for six months. Ajaero had criticised Osifo for rejecting the offer, arguing that the TUC had no right to turn it down. However, Osifo maintained that the TUC had its own position on the offer and that Ajaero could not negotiate on behalf of its members. “Comrade Ajaero does not have the right to negotiate on behalf of organised labour and TUC members. He has the right to negotiate for Nigerian Labour Congress members,” he said. ﻿ Osifo explained that the TUC’s rejection of the allowance was not based on any document signed by Ajaero, saying the congress had communicated its position to the Secretary to the Government of the Federation before the NLC president’s meeting with the Federal Ministry of Labour. “Our rejection was not as a result of the document Ajaero signed. We already took that position with the Secretary to the Government of the Federation earlier on. He never negotiated for it; it was the President of the Federal Republic that gave that,” he said. The TUC president said the congress had proposed a ₦300,000 salary increase but was offered the ₦70,000 transport allowance for six months instead. He said the TUC had rejected the allowance before Ajaero met with the Federal Ministry of Labour and announced the offer. “The ₦70k is something we had rejected earlier before Ajaero had his meeting with the Federal Ministry of Labour,” Osifo said. He maintained that the TUC’s immediate demand was a salary increase, arguing that the Federal Government could raise workers’ pay while discussions on a new minimum wage were pending. “Since it takes time to negotiate minimum wage and there is no law in Nigeria that stipulates maximum wage, some states are currently paying more than the current minimum wage. We can pull the Federal Government to increase the pay of workers,” he said. Osifo said the TUC’s position remained unchanged and had been communicated at a press conference on October 8, 2026. He added that the congress expected minimum wage review discussions to begin in February.
